setup_description: The recommended deployment serves the interface and API from the same Raspberry Pi domain. In development, Docker runs the API and Postgres, then Vite serves the interface.
setup_local_description: Prepare local variables, start the Docker services, then launch the frontend.
setup_credentials_env: Copy apps/api/.env.example to apps/api/.env.local and choose your own Postgres password.
setup_credentials_docker: In Docker Compose, DATABASE_URL uses the postgres host because it is the internal service name.
setup_credentials_production: In production, use the deploy bundle with Caddy. The web image contains a static Vite build served by nginx, with no Vite server running on the Raspberry Pi.
setup_production_same_origin: Serve the interface and API from the same origin to avoid CORS, cross-site cookies, and local-network browser prompts.
setup_production_server_env: Copy deploy/docker-compose.server.yml, deploy/Caddyfile, and deploy/booster-break.env.example to /opt/booster-break, then fill the private booster-break.env file. No secrets are included in the GitHub Container Registry images.
setup_production_slack: Slack OAuth must use the exact Caddy-proxied callback URL, for example https://booster.example.com/api/auth/slack/callback.
setup_production_domains: Caddy serves the interface on https://booster.example.com and proxies the API on /api, which avoids CORS and cross-site cookies.

pvp_rulebook_intro: Three cards, five energy, up to three rounds.
pvp_rule_team: Choose {count} different Pokémon cards from your collection with a maximum budget of {budget} points. Each card plays only one round. Your trio stays secret until revealed.
pvp_rule_energy: You have {energy} energy for the entire duel. Commit 0 to {max} per round. It adds to your card’s power and is spent even on a loss or draw. There are no hidden effects: Feint, Impulse, Assault and Overcharge mean 0, 1, 2 and 3 energy.
pvp_rule_duel: Both players seal a card and intensity. Both choices are revealed together. Strength = power + energy + 1 if one of your card’s types matches an opponent’s printed weakness. The greater strength wins. A tie awards no round and both cards are used. Two round wins, or the highest score after three rounds, wins the duel. Equal scores mean a drawn duel.
pvp_rule_example_detail: Example: power 1 + 2 energy + 1 type advantage = 4. This beats a power 3 card played with no energy.
pvp_rule_elo: Every trainer starts at {rating} Elo. Beating a higher-rated opponent earns more; losing to them costs less. A draw can also adjust Elo. The Trainers tab shows match wins and your three cards with the most round wins. Elo belongs to the duel; card records belong to played rounds.
